It’s been really noticeable for at least the last six months, but honestly, I’ve been like this since I was a kid—teachers always wrote that I “daydream” and “talk too much” on my report cards.

At work, I’m constantly struggling to keep things straight. Balancing drawers, tracking which customer needed what, remembering who I’ve already helped—my notes are all over sticky papers, and I still lose track. I start one task, then something else catches my eye, and I just abandon the first thing without meaning to. Even a coworker walking by or a random thought about what I’m making for dinner will pull my attention away.

I feel like I’m always in motion. On slow days at the bank, I can’t just sit; I’m tapping my foot, spinning in my chair, getting up to “straighten” the brochures.
